title: Meta Plans $300 Muse Charm AI Device, Delays Smartwatch Launch to 2027
summary: Meta plans $300 Muse Charm AI device and delays smartwatch launch to 2027
detailed: Meta is preparing to launch a $300 wearable AI device named Muse Charm while delaying its planned smartwatch release to 2027.
The Muse Charm is priced to attract consumers seeking hands-free, voice-interactive AI experiences without purchasing expensive smart glasses.
The strategic delay of the smartwatch allows Meta to reassess priorities and focus on testing consumer demand through simpler wearable form factors.
Meta is expanding its hardware strategy to build a closer relationship between its proprietary AI services and users' everyday activities.
This hardware expansion matters as tech companies seek new ways to monetize artificial intelligence beyond cloud subscriptions and software apps.
sentences: Meta is reportedly preparing to expand its artificial intelligence hardware ambitions with the planned launch of a $300 Muse Charm AI device, while postponing the release of its smartwatch until 2027.

The reported strategic adjustment highlights Meta’s growing focus on wearable AI products as technology companies increasingly compete to bring artificial intelligence beyond smartphones and into everyday consumer experiences.
The Muse Charm is expected to reflect Meta’s broader vision of integrating AI into personal devices that can offer more convenient, hands-free interactions.

With artificial intelligence increasingly embedded in digital assistants, smart glasses and wearable technology, Meta is looking to strengthen its position in a market where convenience, accessibility and functionality could determine consumer adoption.
At a reported price of $300, the Muse Charm could occupy an interesting position in the emerging AI hardware market.

The device’s pricing would place it within reach of consumers willing to experiment with new AI-powered products without necessarily purchasing more expensive smart glasses or advanced wearable devices.
However, the success of the product will likely depend on its functionality, battery life, user experience and ability to deliver meaningful benefits beyond existing smartphones.
Meta has been investing heavily in artificial intelligence, including developing AI models, expanding its computing infrastructure and integrating AI assistants across its social media platforms.
Hardware represents another important dimension of that strategy, allowing the company to potentially build a closer relationship between its AI services and users’ everyday activities.
The decision to delay the smartwatch launch until 2027, meanwhile, suggests Meta may be reassessing its product development priorities, timelines or competitive positioning.
Smartwatches remain a highly competitive segment dominated by established technology companies with sophisticated ecosystems, including Apple and Samsung.
Entering the market successfully would require Meta to differentiate its product through software, health and fitness capabilities, connectivity, design or AI integration.
Rather than rushing multiple hardware products to market, Meta could be prioritising the Muse Charm as an opportunity to test consumer demand for a new category of AI-powered wearables.
The strategy may also allow the company to refine its technological capabilities and gather feedback before introducing a more complex smartwatch product.
The broader AI hardware market is attracting significant interest as companies seek new ways to monetise artificial intelligence beyond subscriptions, cloud services and advertising.

Devices that offer voice interaction, contextual assistance and seamless connectivity could eventually become important components of digital ecosystems, particularly as AI assistants become increasingly capable.
However, consumer enthusiasm remains uncertain.
Many AI hardware products have struggled to demonstrate compelling use cases, with users often questioning whether standalone devices offer enough value to justify additional spending.
Meta will therefore need to ensure the Muse Charm delivers practical functionality rather than simply introducing another gadget into an already crowded consumer electronics market.
The reported $300 Muse Charm plan and smartwatch delay underscore Meta’s evolving hardware strategy.

As competition intensifies, the company appears focused on finding the right combination of AI innovation, consumer appeal and timing to establish a stronger presence in the next generation of wearable technology.
